items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee confirms the name 'Walter Davis' but the subsequent narrative describes a 'little kid' playing with a tree branch, whom the interviewee gave drumsticks to. There is no evidence in the text that the 'little kid' is Walter Davis, nor any other interaction between Terry Clark and Walter

ctx.x: Walter Bishop. Walter Davis, yeah. So a whole bunch of us were playing, and this little kid was in the back of the bandstand, and he had a tree, a piece of a tree. Ding ding ding ding ding. He was keeping time. Just a piece of old raggedy tree branch. But he was really – you could tell he was really into it. At the first intermission – I kept watching this kid, and I took these two – these drum sticks out of my case, and I gave them to this kid. I said, “Try these, man. You watch the drummer, and do what he…

sure – I don’t – I wish it were possible that I could keep up with his career from that point, but I’ll bet you this kid is into giving vent to his feelings now. But he otherwise wouldn’t have had a chance. The kids back in those days didn’t have the chance, so that’s why you still see some kids who are creative, and I think it has to do with their inner spirits and with their support from the family, because a lot of those same kids go the other route, to the junk route, and they all end up following each other,…
